samples.claim: has_spilled_row_lineage is OR of RowIdMeta::Column and the two RowDatasetVersionMeta::Column states. row_lineage_file(field_id) scans only base files for fields.contains(id), returns None if absent, first file if unique, or CorruptFile naming the second carrier path and fragment/field IDs if duplicated across files. It accepts arbitrary i32 input and does not reject repeated IDs within one file or inspect column_indices/metadata state. Missing carrier is not itself an error in this lookup.

635 |     /// Whether any of this fragment's row lineage sequences lives in a data
636 |     /// file column rather than inline.
637 |     pub fn has_spilled_row_lineage(&self) -> bool {
638 |         matches!(self.row_id_meta, Some(RowIdMeta::Column))
639 |             || matches!(
640 |                 self.created_at_version_meta,
641 |                 Some(RowDatasetVersionMeta::Column)
642 |             )
643 |             || matches!(
644 |                 self.last_updated_at_version_meta,

650 |     /// `field_id`, which is the one entry of [`Self::files`] whose fields carry

652 |     /// it is spilled is corruption; so is more than one file carrying the id,
653 |     /// which this reports as an error.

669 |         Ok(file)

samples.claim: validate first rejects every nonfinite f64 field, in order initial,min,max,decrease,increment,threshold, with InvalidInput naming field/value. Comments explain that NaN evades comparisons and can disable a downstream token bucket or panic duration conversion; those downstream behaviors are rationale, not code implemented here. NaN and infinities are rejected even for the optional maximum ceiling; finite zero disables it.

102 |     /// Validate that the configuration values are sensible.
103 |     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
104 |         // Reject NaN and infinity first. The sign and ordering checks below
105 |         // compare with `<`/`>`, which are `false` for NaN and for a `+inf` on
106 |         // a field with no opposing bound, so a non-finite rate would otherwise
107 |         // slip through and silently disable throttling (a NaN rate makes the
108 |         // token bucket refill to full on every acquire) or, with a zero burst
109 |         // capacity, panic in `Duration::from_secs_f64`.
110 |         for (name, value) in [
111 |             ("initial_rate", self.initial_rate),

113 |             ("max_rate", self.max_rate),
114 |             ("decrease_factor", self.decrease_factor),
115 |             ("additive_increment", self.additive_increment),
116 |             ("throttle_threshold", self.throttle_threshold),
117 |         ] {
118 |             if !value.is_finite() {
119 |                 return Err(crate::Error::invalid_input(format!(
120 |                     "{name} must be finite, got {value}"

samples.claim: from_bitmap assumes bitmap.len fits u32 but does not checked-convert it. Iterates bytes with valid_bits=min(span-offset,8); ORs bits beyond logical length to present via checked_shl so padding cannot open a hole. All-present byte closes an open run at byte start; all-missing byte opens/continues a run. The compacted-table byte distribution is a performance rationale in comments, not measured here.
